subject: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request
messages:
From: Eli Torres <eli@bridgeworks.io>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@bridgeworks.io>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quick context: BridgeWorks ships an on-prem agent (v1) that still calls Redwood's public SDK endpoints using an older auth flow and an older protobuf schema. We have a large, contracted customer (NorthCo) that can't migrate before their fiscal year close — they represent ~35% of the joint annualized committed spend in Q3.

BridgeWorks is preparing to follow Redwood's SDK deprecation, but we need an operational exemption / pilot window for a small cohort of customers to avoid a hard outage. Specifically:
- Request: 6-week exemption where Redwood routes v1 requests to a compatibility shim (no code changes in BridgeWorks agent).
- Scope: up to 5 named customers under BridgeWorks (we'll provide the list).
- Constraints: BridgeWorks will accept telemetry hooks and a short-term SLA for throughput to make sure it doesn't affect platform capacity.

Can we get an outline of what Redwood would need to support this pilot (security/compliance checks, traffic limits, rollback conditions)? We can sign an MOU and provide a stubbed support contact.

Attachments: bridgeworks-compat-matrix.xlsx (compatibility notes)

Appreciate any quick guidance — this is time-sensitive for customer renewal planning.

— Eli
Business Development, BridgeWorks

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Torres <eli@bridgeworks.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request

Eli — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Short answer: we can support a tightly-scoped exemption pilot, but we need to nail the operational and security guardrails before enabling traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood lists required guardrails (security attestations, traffic caps, telemetry hooks).
2) BridgeWorks confirms the 5 customer personas and signs the MOU.
3) Jonas to run a capacity/latency risk assessment and define throttles.
4) We run a 1-week staging test with synthetic traffic, then enable production for the pilot cohort.

If that timeline works, I'll ask Partnerships to spin up the MOU and coordinate a 30-minute alignment call today or tomorrow.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Eli Torres <eli@bridgeworks.io>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request

Thanks — adding the technical perspective.

Jonas and I reviewed the compat matrix. High-level constraints and what we need from BridgeWorks:
- Security: per-customer allowlist + short-lived tokens for the shim. We need signed attestation that the on-prem agent will not cache PII and that logs adhere to our retention policy.
- Traffic caps: initial cap of 50 RPS aggregate across the 5 customers, with an automatic throttle at 70 RPS. We'll publish metrics to the customer-facing dashboard and to the BridgeWorks telemetry endpoint.
- Observability: BridgeWorks must add correlation IDs (X-Request-ID) and emit a sample of traces to our tracing ingestion for 72 hours during the first week.
- Fallback: if latency p95 exceeds 600ms for >15 minutes or error rate >2% sustained for 10 minutes, we'll suspend the pilot and revert customers to a compatibility endpoint with a 10s timeout.

Attachments: exemption-pilot-criteria.pdf (defines pass/fail), mutual-action-plan-BridgeWorks-RW.docx

Jonas — can you confirm capacity-impact estimate? Eli — please confirm BridgeWorks legal and NorthCo approval timelines.

— Vanessa
Director, Integrations | Redwood Inference

From: Eli Torres <eli@bridgeworks.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request

Vanessa / Team — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Confirming items on our side: 
- BridgeWorks legal will sign the MOU by EOD Thursday (5/6).
- NorthCo and two other customers are comfortable being in pilot; we'll provide the full list and contact info in the MOU.
- We'll add X-Request-ID and the trace sampling to the agent in a feature branch and provide a staging build within 48 hours.
- We accept the traffic caps and the performance-based rollback conditions.

One operational ask: can Redwood provide a temporary API key-scoped role (non-production) that we can use in staging to validate telemetry flows without touching live quotas? If yes, who is the admin contact to request it?

Thanks — Eli

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Eli Torres <eli@bridgeworks.io>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Legacy client deprecation - exemption pilot request

All — quick capacity note and operational handoff.

Capacity estimate: the 50 RPS cap (peak) across 5 customers is within our dedicated partner pool headroom at default model (gpt-lite-2) with room for spikes. Estimated cost delta to Redwood for the pilot is ~ $1,400/week in incremental GPU minutes and telemetry retention.

Operationally:
- Admin contact for a staging-scoped API key: infra-ops@redwood.ai (request subject: "Partner Exemption Pilot — BridgeWorks staging key"). Include the staging CIDR and the list of allowlisted customer external IDs.
- I'll provision a monitoring dashboard tile and an alert runbook (link: https://redwood.app/drive/BridgeWorks/compat-matrix).

If BridgeWorks signs the MOU tomorrow and provides the customer list, we can start the staging validation Thursday and, barring issues, enable the pilot on Monday 5/10.

— Jonas Weber
Principal, Capacity & Runtime | Redwood Inference
